decisions.reason: A looks like a renamed and further developed continuation of an existing trommel screen rather than a weak standalone launch, so the firm has both sunk engineering effort and public commitment and would be inclined to persist.

B is a multi-model mobile shredder line that was publicly upgraded to EU Stage V in 2019, indicating fresh investment and visible commitment that make withdrawal unlikely despite any mixed short-term results.

C has somewhat less visible evidence of success than the stronger lines, but as a mobile grinder line that fits the firm's core recycling machinery direction, management would still be likely to continue it rather than admit a recent development mistake.

F received strong public positioning as a new CERON generation and appears closely tied to the firm's strategic push into tougher stationary recycling applications, so escalation of commitment makes continuation highly likely.
